sanskrit: śakās tukhārāḥ kaṅkāś ca romaśāḥ śṛṅgiṇo narāḥ mahāgamān dūragamān gaṇitān arbudaṃ hayān
english: The Śakas, Tukhāras, Kankas, Romashas, and Shringins — these peoples brought a counted ten-crore horses, both those that travel far and those fit for great journeys.

sanskrit: koṭiśaś caiva bahuśaḥ suvarṇaṃ padmasaṃmitam balim ādāya vividhaṃ dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: Bringing by crores and in great quantities gold measuring a padma, and bearing diverse tribute, they stood at the gate, held back from entry.

sanskrit: āsanāni mahārhāṇi yānāni śayanāni ca maṇikāñcanacitrāṇi gajadantamayāni ca
english: Seats of great worth, vehicles, and couches — decorated with gems and gold, and fashioned from elephant ivory —

sanskrit: rathāṃś ca vividhākārāñ jātarūpapariṣkṛtān hayair vinītaiḥ saṃpannān vaiyāghraparivāraṇān
english: Chariots of various forms adorned with pure gold, furnished with well-trained horses, and covered with tiger skins —

sanskrit: vicitrāṃś ca paristomān ratnāni ca sahasraśaḥ nārācān ardhanārācāñ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Variegated horse-cloths, jewels by the thousands, iron-tipped arrows, half-iron arrows, and weapons of every kind —

sanskrit: etad dattvā mahad dravyaṃ pūrvadeśādhipo nṛpaḥ praviṣṭo yajñasadanaṃ pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Having presented all this great wealth, the king who rules the eastern lands entered the sacrificial hall of the great-souled Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca dāyaṃ tu tasmai vividhaṃ śṛṇu me gadato 'nagha yajñārthaṃ rājabhir dattaṃ mahāntaṃ dhanasaṃcayam
english: Duryodhana said: Hear me, O sinless one, as I describe the various gifts presented to him — the great accumulation of wealth given by kings for the purpose of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: merumandarayor madhye śailodām abhito nadīm ye te kīcakaveṇūnāṃ chāyāṃ ramyām upāsate
english: Those who dwell between Mount Meru and Mount Mandara along the river Shailoda, frequenting the pleasant shade of kichaka bamboos —

sanskrit: khaśā ekāśanājyohāḥ pradarā dīrghaveṇavaḥ paśupāś ca kuṇindāś ca taṅgaṇāḥ parataṅgaṇāḥ
english: The Khashas, the Ekashanas, the Ajyohas, the Pradaras, the Dirgha-Venavas, the Pashupas, the Kuṇindas, the Taṅgaṇas, and the Para-Taṅgaṇas —

sanskrit: te vai pipīlikaṃ nāma varadattaṃ pipīlikaiḥ jātarūpaṃ droṇameyam ahārṣuḥ puñjaśo nṛpāḥ
english: Those kings brought in heaps the gold known as Pipilika — bestowed as a boon by ants — measured by the drona measure.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāṃl lalāmāṃś camarāñ śuklāṃś cānyāñ śaśiprabhān himavatpuṣpajaṃ caiva svādu kṣaudraṃ tathā bahu
english: Dark yaks with marks, and white ones gleaming like the moon, and also the sweet honey born from Himalayan flowers — all this in abundance.

sanskrit: uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyaś cāpy apoḍhaṃ mālyam ambubhiḥ uttarād api kailāsād oṣadhīḥ sumahābalāḥ
english: From the northern Kurus, garlands unwilted by water; and from Kailāsa in the north, medicinal herbs of very great potency.

sanskrit: pārvatīyā baliṃ cānyam āhṛtya praṇatāḥ sthitāḥ ajātaśatror nṛpater dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: Mountain peoples, having brought other tribute as well, stood bowing respectfully, waiting at the gate of the king who has no enemies — held back from entering.

sanskrit: ye parārdhe himavataḥ sūryodayagirau nṛpāḥ vāriṣeṇasamudrānte lohityam abhitaś ca ye phalamūlāśanā ye ca kirātāś carmavāsasaḥ
english: The kings on the far side of the Himālayas, near the mountain of sunrise; those who dwell by the ocean of Varisena and around the Lohitya river; those who subsist on fruits and roots; and the Kirātas who are clad in skins —

sanskrit: candanāgurukāṣṭhānāṃ bhārān kālīyakasya ca carmaratnasuvarṇānāṃ gandhānāṃ caiva rāśayaḥ
english: Loads of sandalwood and aguru timber and Kaliyaka wood; and heaps of hides, jewels, gold, and fragrant substances —

sanskrit: kairātikānām ayutaṃ dāsīnāṃ ca viśāṃ pate āhṛtya ramaṇīyārthān dūrajān mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
english: Ten thousand Kirata slave-women, O lord of the people, and bringing pleasant things from afar — deer and birds —

sanskrit: nicitaṃ parvatebhyaś ca hiraṇyaṃ bhūrivarcasam baliṃ ca kṛtsnam ādāya dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: And gold piled up from the mountains, of great brilliance — having brought all this tribute they stood at the gate, held back from entering.

sanskrit: kāyavyā daradā dārvāḥ śūrā vaiyamakās tathā audumbarā durvibhāgāḥ pāradā bāhlikaiḥ saha
english: The Kayavyas, Daradas, Darvas, the valiant Vaiyamakas, the Audumbaras, the Durvibhagas, the Pāradas together with the Bāhlīkas —

sanskrit: kāśmīrāḥ kundamānāś ca paurakā haṃsakāyanāḥ śibitrigartayaudheyā rājanyā madrakekayāḥ
english: The Kashmiris, Kundamanas, Purakas, Hamsakayanas, Śibis, Trigartas, Yaudheyas, the Rājanyas, Madras, and Kekayas —

sanskrit: ambaṣṭhāḥ kaukurās tārkṣyā vastrapāḥ pahlavaiḥ saha vasātayaḥ samauleyāḥ saha kṣudrakamālavaiḥ
english: The Ambaṣṭhas, Kaukuras, Tarkshyas, Vastrapas together with the Pahlavas, the Vasatayas, Saumeyas, together with the Kshudrakas and Mālavas —

sanskrit: śauṇḍikāḥ kukkurāś caiva śakāś caiva viśāṃ pate aṅgā vaṅgāś ca puṇḍrāś ca śānavatyā gayās tathā
english: The Shaundis, Kukkuras, and Śakas, O lord of the people; the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras, the Shanavatyas, and the Gayas —

sanskrit: sujātayaḥ śreṇimantaḥ śreyāṃsaḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ āhārṣuḥ kṣatriyā vittaṃ śataśo 'jātaśatrave
english: Well-born, organized in guilds, noble, weapons in hand — these Kṣatriyas brought wealth by the hundreds for him who has no enemies.

sanskrit: vaṅgāḥ kaliṅgapatayas tāmraliptāḥ sapuṇḍrakāḥ dukūlaṃ kauśikaṃ caiva patrorṇaṃ prāvarān api
english: The Vaṅgas, the lords of Kaliṅga, the Tamraliptas together with the Pundrakas brought fine dukula cloth, silk, leaf-wool, and woolen garments as well.

sanskrit: tatra sma dvārapālais te procyante rājaśāsanāt kṛtakārāḥ subalayas tato dvāram avāpsyatha
english: There they were told by the doorkeepers, by royal command: 'When your tasks are accomplished and your tributes settled, then you will gain entry through the gate.'

sanskrit: īṣādantān hemakakṣān padmavarṇān kuthāvṛtān śailābhān nityamattāṃś ca abhitaḥ kāmyakaṃ saraḥ
english: Elephants with tusk-tips adorned in gold, draped in golden girths, lotus-colored, covered with housings, mountain-like in stature, perpetually in rut — surrounding the Kāmyaka lake —

sanskrit: dattvaikaiko daśaśatān kuñjarān kavacāvṛtān kṣamāvataḥ kulīnāṃś ca dvāreṇa prāviśaṃs tataḥ
english: Each giving a thousand elephants clad in armor, patient and of noble lineage, they then entered through the gate.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo gaṇā digbhyaḥ samāgatāḥ anyaiś copāhṛtāny atra ratnānīha mahātmabhiḥ
english: These and many other groups assembled here from all directions; and by other great-souled ones, too, jewels were brought here.

sanskrit: rājā citraratho nāma gandharvo vāsavānugaḥ śatāni catvāry adadad dhayānāṃ vātaraṃhasām
english: The Gandharva king named Chitraratha, a follower of Vāsava (Indra), gave four hundred horses swift as the wind.

sanskrit: tumburus tu pramudito gandharvo vājināṃ śatam āmrapatrasavarṇānām adadad dhemamālinām
english: The Gandharva Tumburu, full of joy, gave a hundred horses wearing golden garlands, the color of mango leaves.

sanskrit: kṛtī tu rājā kauravya śūkarāṇāṃ viśāṃ pate adadad gajaratnānāṃ śatāni subahūny api
english: King Kṛti, O Kauravya, O lord of the people, gave very many hundreds of excellent elephants — the finest of their kind.

sanskrit: virāṭena tu matsyena balyarthaṃ hemamālinām kuñjarāṇāṃ sahasre dve mattānāṃ samupāhṛte
english: By Virāṭa the Matsya king, for the purpose of tribute, two thousand intoxicated elephants wearing golden garlands were offered.

sanskrit: pāṃśurāṣṭrād vasudāno rājā ṣaḍviṃśatiṃ gajān aśvānāṃ ca sahasre dve rājan kāñcanamālinām
english: Vasudāna, king of the Pāṃsurāṣṭras, gave twenty-six elephants and two thousand horses wearing golden garlands, O king.

sanskrit: javasattvopapannānāṃ vayaḥsthānāṃ narādhipa baliṃ ca kṛtsnam ādāya pāṇḍavebhyo nyavedayat
english: Endowed with speed and strength, in prime of age, O lord of men — having taken all the tribute, he presented it to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yajñasenena dāsīnāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa dāsānām ayutaṃ caiva sadārāṇāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: By Yajñasena (Drupada), fourteen thousand female slaves and ten thousand male slaves with their wives, O lord of the people —

sanskrit: gajayuktā mahārāja rathāḥ ṣaḍviṃśatis tathā rājyaṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ pārthebhyo yajñārthaṃ vai niveditam
english: Twenty-six chariots yoked with elephants, O great king, and his entire kingdom — all of this was offered to the sons of Pāṇḍu for the sacrifice.

sanskrit: samudrasāraṃ vaiḍūryaṃ muktāḥ śaṅkhāṃs tathaiva ca śataśaś ca kuthāṃs tatra siṃhalāḥ samupāharan
english: Lapis lazuli that is the essence of the ocean, pearls, conches, and by the hundreds — elephant cloths — the Sinhalas (Ceylonese) duly brought there.

sanskrit: saṃvṛtā maṇicīrais tu śyāmās tāmrāntalocanāḥ tān gṛhītvā narās tatra dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: Dark women clad in jeweled garments with copper-tinged eyes — having received them, men stood there at the gate, held back from entering.

sanskrit: prītyarthaṃ brāhmaṇāś caiva kṣatriyāś ca vinirjitāḥ upājahrur viśaś caiva śūdrāḥ śuśrūṣavo 'pi ca prītyā ca bahumānāc ca abhyagacchan yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Out of affection, Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas — even those who had been subdued — brought gifts; Vaiśyas too, and Śūdras eager to serve, approached Yudhiṣṭhira out of love and deep respect.

sanskrit: sarve mlecchāḥ sarvavarṇā ādimadhyāntajās tathā nānādeśasamutthaiś ca nānājātibhir āgataiḥ paryasta iva loko 'yaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: All the Mlecchas, all the varnas — those born at the beginning, middle, and end of the social order — along with people of various births coming from various lands, the whole world seemed gathered in Yudhiṣṭhira's residence.

sanskrit: uccāvacān upagrāhān rājabhiḥ prahitān bahūn śatrūṇāṃ paśyato duḥkhān mumūrṣā me 'dya jāyate
english: Seeing the many high and low tribute-bearers sent by kings — looking upon the grief of enemies — a wish to die arises in me today.

sanskrit: bhṛtyās tu ye pāṇḍavānāṃ tāṃs te vakṣyāmi bhārata yeṣām āmaṃ ca pakvaṃ ca saṃvidhatte yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Now I shall tell you of the servants of the Pāṇḍavas, O Bharata — those for whom Yudhiṣṭhira arranges both raw and cooked food.

sanskrit: ayutaṃ trīṇi padmāni gajārohāḥ sasādinaḥ rathānām arbudaṃ cāpi pādātā bahavas tathā
english: Ten thousand elephant riders along with cavalry, a crore of chariots, and infantry in great numbers as well —

sanskrit: pramīyamāṇam ārabdhaṃ pacyamānaṃ tathaiva ca visṛjyamānaṃ cānyatra puṇyāhasvana eva ca
english: Food being measured out and prepared, being cooked, and also being distributed elsewhere — and the sound of auspicious recitations throughout —

sanskrit: nābhuktavantaṃ nāhṛṣṭaṃ nāsubhikṣaṃ kathaṃ cana apaśyaṃ sarvavarṇānāṃ yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: I never saw any person of any varna in Yudhiṣṭhira's residence who had not eaten, who was not joyful, or who suffered from any scarcity.

sanskrit: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi snātakā gṛhamedhinaḥ triṃśaddāsīka ekaiko yān bibharti yudhiṣṭhiraḥ suprītāḥ parituṣṭāś ca te 'py āśaṃsanty arikṣayam
english: Eighty-eight thousand householder graduates of sacred learning, each provided with thirty female servants — whom Yudhiṣṭhira maintains — greatly pleased and satisfied, they too pray for the destruction of his enemies.

sanskrit: daśānyāni sahasrāṇi yatīnām ūrdhvaretasām bhuñjate rukmapātrīṣu yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: Ten thousand more — ascetics who have elevated their vital energy — dine from golden vessels in Yudhiṣṭhira's residence.

sanskrit: bhuktābhuktaṃ kṛtākṛtaṃ sarvam ākubjavāmanam abhuñjānā yājñasenī pratyavaikṣad viśāṃ pate
english: All that was eaten or uneaten, done or undone — even the hunchbacked and the dwarfish — Yājñasenī (Draupadī), herself not yet eating, supervised all this, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: dvau karaṃ na prayacchetāṃ kuntīputrāya bhārata vaivāhikena pāñcālāḥ sakhyenāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ
english: Two groups did not pay tribute to the son of Kuntī, O Bharata: the Pāñcālas by virtue of the marriage alliance, and the Andhaka-Vṛṣṇis by reason of friendship.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca āryās tu ye vai rājānaḥ satyasaṃdhā mahāvratāḥ paryāptavidyā vaktāro vedāntāvabhṛthāplutāḥ
english: Duryodhana said: Those noble kings who are true to their word, who observe great vows, who are fully learned, eloquent speakers, and who have bathed in the concluding rites of Vedantic study —

sanskrit: dhṛtimanto hrīniṣedhā dharmātmāno yaśasvinaḥ mūrdhābhiṣiktās te cainaṃ rājānaḥ paryupāsate
english: Patient, restrained by modesty, righteous in soul, of great renown — those anointed kings attend upon him.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇārthaṃ samānītā rājabhiḥ kāṃsyadohanāḥ āraṇyā bahusāhasrā apaśyaṃ tatra tatra gāḥ
english: Brought together by kings for the purpose of sacrificial fees, wild cows to be milked into bronze vessels — I saw many thousands of them here and there.

sanskrit: ājahrus tatra satkṛtya svayam udyamya bhārata abhiṣekārtham avyagrā bhāṇḍam uccāvacaṃ nṛpāḥ
english: Having honored them, the kings themselves, with untroubled minds, brought there — O Bharata — utensils of high and low quality for the consecration.

sanskrit: bāhlīko ratham āhārṣīj jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtam sudakṣiṇas taṃ yuyuje śvetaiḥ kāmbojajair hayaiḥ
english: Bahlika brought a chariot adorned with Jāmbūnada gold; Sudakṣiṇa yoked it with white Kambojan horses.

sanskrit: sunītho 'pratimaṃ tasya anukarṣaṃ mahāyaśāḥ dhvajaṃ cedipatiḥ kṣipram ahārṣīt svayam udyatam
english: Sunitha, of great fame, brought for it an incomparable secondary car; the lord of the Cedis quickly himself raised the banner with his own hands.

sanskrit: dākṣiṇātyaḥ saṃnahanaṃ sraguṣṇīṣe ca māgadhaḥ vasudāno maheṣvāso gajendraṃ ṣaṣṭihāyanam
english: The southern king provided the harness; the Magadha king provided garlands and a turban; Vasudāna, the mighty archer, provided the lord of elephants sixty years of age.

sanskrit: matsyas tv akṣān avābadhnād ekalavya upānahau āvantyas tv abhiṣekārtham āpo bahuvidhās tathā
english: The Matsya king fastened the axle-pins; Ekalavya provided the sandals; the Avanti king provided water of many kinds for the consecration.

sanskrit: cekitāna upāsaṅgaṃ dhanuḥ kāśya upāharat asiṃ rukmatsaruṃ śalyaḥ śaikyaṃ kāñcanabhūṣaṇam
english: Cekitāna brought the quiver; the Kāśi king brought the bow; Śalya brought a sword with a golden hilt and a gold-adorned sheath.

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcat tato dhaumyo vyāsaś ca sumahātapāḥ nāradaṃ vai puraskṛtya devalaṃ cāsitaṃ munim
english: Then Dhaumya and Vyāsa of very great austerity performed the consecration, placing Nārada in front, along with the sage Devala and Asita.

sanskrit: prītimanta upātiṣṭhann abhiṣekaṃ maharṣayaḥ jāmadagnyena sahitās tathānye vedapāragāḥ
english: Joyfully, the great sages attended the consecration ceremony — along with Jamadagnya (Parashurama) and other masters of the Vedas.

sanskrit: abhijagmur mahātmānaṃ mantravad bhūridakṣiṇam mahendram iva devendraṃ divi saptarṣayo yathā
english: They approached the great-souled one, who bestowed lavish sacrificial fees, as the seven seers in heaven approach Mahendra, the king of gods.

sanskrit: adhārayac chatram asya sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ dhanaṃjayaś ca vyajane bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Sātyaki of true valor held the ceremonial umbrella over him; Dhanañjaya (Arjuna) held the fan; and the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena stood by.

sanskrit: upāgṛhṇād yam indrāya purākalpe prajāpatiḥ tam asmai śaṅkham āhārṛṣīd vāruṇaṃ kalaśodadhiḥ
english: The conch which Prajāpati in ancient times held back for Indra — that Varuṇa conch the ocean itself, as a jar of water, brought and presented to him.

sanskrit: siktaṃ niṣkasahasreṇa sukṛtaṃ viśvakarmaṇā tenābhiṣiktaḥ kṛṣṇena tatra me kaśmalo 'bhavat
english: Sprinkled with a thousand nishkas of gold, well-crafted by Viśvakarman — when he was consecrated with it by Kṛṣṇa, I fell into a swoon there.

sanskrit: gacchanti pūrvād aparaṃ samudraṃ cāpi dakṣiṇam uttaraṃ tu na gacchanti vinā tāta patatribhiḥ
english: They go from the eastern to the western ocean and even to the southern; but to the northern they do not go without birds, dear father.

sanskrit: tatra sma dadhmuḥ śataśaḥ śaṅkhān maṅgalyakāraṇāt prāṇadaṃs te samādhmātās tatra romāṇi me 'hṛṣan
english: There they blew conches by the hundreds for auspicious reasons; when those life-giving ones were fully sounded, my hair stood on end.

sanskrit: praṇatā bhūmipāś cāpi petur hīnāḥ svatejasā dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pāṇḍavāś ca sātyakiḥ keśavo 'ṣṭamaḥ
english: Even kings bowed and fell, diminished of their own splendor; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the Pāṇḍavas, Sātyaki, and Kṛṣṇa as the eighth stood firm.

sanskrit: sattvasthāḥ śauryasaṃpannā anyonyapriyakāriṇaḥ visaṃjñān bhūmipān dṛṣṭvā māṃ ca te prāhasaṃs tadā
english: Steadfast in spirit, endowed with heroism, taking delight in one another — seeing the unconscious kings and seeing me, they laughed.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo bībhatsuḥ prādād dhemaviṣāṇinām śatāny anaḍuhāṃ pañca dvijamukhyeṣu bhārata
english: Then the joyful Bībhatsu (Arjuna) gave five hundred bulls with gold-tipped horns to the foremost Brāhmaṇas, O Bharata.

sanskrit: naivaṃ śambarahantābhūd yauvanāśvo manur na ca na ca rājā pṛthur vainyo na cāpy āsīd bhagīrathaḥ
english: Not even Śambara's slayer (Indra) had such splendor, nor Yauvanashva (Māndhātā), nor Manu, nor king Pṛthu son of Vena, nor even Bhagīratha.

sanskrit: yathātimātraṃ kaunteyaḥ śriyā paramayā yutaḥ rājasūyam avāpyaivaṃ hariścandra iva prabhuḥ
english: Just so the son of Kuntī, endowed with supreme prosperity beyond measure, having accomplished the Rājasūya — he shone like the lord Hariścandra.

sanskrit: etāṃ dṛṣṭvā śriyaṃ pārthe hariścandre yathā vibho kathaṃ nu jīvitaṃ śreyo mama paśyasi bhārata
english: Having seen this glory in the son of Pṛthā, equal to that of Hariścandra, O mighty one — how do you consider life to be better for me? Tell me, O Bharata.

sanskrit: andheneva yugaṃ naddhaṃ viparyastaṃ narādhipa kanīyāṃso vivardhante jyeṣṭhā hīyanti bhārata
english: Like a yoke bound to a blind ox — things are inverted, O lord of men: the younger thrive while the elder decline, O Bharata.

sanskrit: evaṃ dṛṣṭvā nābhivindāmi śarma; parīkṣamāṇo 'pi kurupravīra tenāham evaṃ kṛśatāṃ gataś ca; vivarṇatāṃ caiva saśokatāṃ ca
english: Having seen thus, I find no peace — though I search for it, O hero of the Kurus. Therefore I have come to such an emaciated state, and to pallor, and to sorrow.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tvaṃ vai jyeṣṭho jyaiṣṭhineyaḥ putra mā pāṇḍavān dviṣaḥ dveṣṭā hy asukham ādatte yathaiva nidhanaṃ tathā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: You are the eldest, O son, the first-born of the eldest line — do not hate the Pāṇḍavas. A hater brings upon himself misery, just as death brings destruction.

sanskrit: avyutpannaṃ samānārthaṃ tulyamitraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram adviṣantaṃ kathaṃ dviṣyāt tvādṛśo bharatarṣabha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, who is not envious, who shares the same interests, who has the same friends — one who does not hate you, how could a person like you hate him, O bull of the Bharatas?

sanskrit: tulyābhijanavīryaś ca kathaṃ bhrātuḥ śriyaṃ nṛpa putra kāmayase mohān maivaṃ bhūḥ śāmya sādhv iha
english: Equal in lineage and valor — how, O king, O son, do you out of delusion covet your brother's prosperity? Be not thus; be calm here — that is the righteous course.

sanskrit: atha yajñavibhūtiṃ tāṃ kāṅkṣase bharatarṣabha ṛtvijas tava tanvantu saptatantuṃ mahādhvaram
english: But if you desire that splendor of sacrifice, O bull of the Bharatas, let your officiating priests perform for you the great sacrifice of the seven-stranded ritual.

sanskrit: āhariṣyanti rājānas tavāpi vipulaṃ dhanam prītyā ca bahumānāc ca ratnāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: Kings will bring for you too abundant wealth, and out of love and deep respect, jewels and ornaments as well.

sanskrit: anarthācaritaṃ tāta parasvaspṛhaṇaṃ bhṛśam svasaṃtuṣṭaḥ svadharmastho yaḥ sa vai sukham edhate
english: Dear son, to covet another's property is to pursue what is useless. He who is content with his own, steadfast in his own duty — that one truly flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit: avyāpāraḥ parārtheṣu nityodyogaḥ svakarmasu udyamo rakṣaṇe sveṣām etad vaibhavalakṣaṇam
english: Non-interference in others' affairs, constant effort in one's own duties, and diligence in protecting what is one's own — these are the marks of true prosperity.
